moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Identify Testim's four debugging tools: Debugging Controls, Debugging Helper Panels, JavaScript Code Debugging, and Recording New Steps to Resolve Bugs.
Pause, continue, and step through a running test to inspect its behavior.
Distinguish manual breakpoints from virtual breakpoints.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The four Testim debugging tools, at a glance

elements.title: Testim Debugging Tools
items: A. Debugging Controls — Pause/Continue, step-by-step execution, manual and virtual breakpoints. Covered in depth below.
B. Debugging Helper Panels — supporting panels that surface richer per-step context during a debugging session. Covered below.
C. JavaScript Code Debugging — the dedicated workflow for stepping through the hand-written or AI-generated code inside custom action/validation/CLI steps. Covered below.

D. Recording New Steps to Resolve Bugs — inserting missing or corrected steps into an existing test at a specific position, without re-recording the whole test. Covered in depth in its own 'Recording new steps to resolve bugs' module.

elements.text: These four tools form a natural workflow: use Debugging Controls and Helper Panels to isolate exactly where and why a test broke, drop into JS Code Debugging if the culprit is a custom step's code, then use Recording New Steps to fix the test itself once the root cause is clear.

bulletPoints: Debugging Helper Panels + JS Code Debugging = deeper per-step and per-code-step inspection.
Recording New Steps to Resolve Bugs = fixing the test once you know what's wrong (see its own module).

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Debugging Helper Panels and JS Code Debugging

elements.description: Supporting panels available during a debugging session that surface additional context around a step — building on Pause/Continue, breakpoints, and step-by-step execution with a richer inspection surface for diagnosing exactly why a step behaved the way it did.

A dedicated debugging workflow for custom JavaScript steps (custom actions, custom validations, CLI actions) — since these steps run hand-written or AI-generated code rather than a predefined action, they need their own debugging path distinct from the generic step-level breakpoint tools covered above.

bulletPoints: Debug Helper panels add richer step-level inspection during a debugging session.
JS Code Debugging is the dedicated path for diagnosing custom JavaScript step code specifically — generic breakpoints don't step through that code.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Debugging Controls: pausing and stepping through a test

elements.description: Pauses test execution at any point in the editor — the run stops at the nearest step when clicked — after which Continue resumes execution from that exact location until the test ends.

To run step-by-step, click the dropdown next to the Play button and select 'Run locally step by step', then use the 'Play Next Step' button to execute one step at a time — letting you inspect state after each individual action rather than watching the whole test run at full speed.

Breakpoints pause execution at various stages. Manual breakpoints are explicitly set by the user at a chosen step. Virtual breakpoints are created automatically by the system when debugging controls are used — such as step into, step out, step over, and pause — without the user having to set them by hand.

elements.text: The breakpoint manager panel lists and manages all breakpoints in a test, giving a single place to review where execution will pause before a debugging session starts.

bulletPoints: Pause stops at the nearest step; Continue resumes from exactly there.
Step-by-step run: dropdown next to Play → 'Run locally step by step' → 'Play Next Step'.
Manual breakpoints = user-set; virtual breakpoints = auto-created by debugging controls (step into/out/over, pause).

examPitfalls.title: Assuming all breakpoints must be manually placed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Not realizing that using debugging controls like step into/out/over automatically creates breakpoints of their own.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Virtual breakpoints are created automatically by the system whenever debugging controls (step into, step out, step over, pause) are used — they exist alongside any manual breakpoints you set yourself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the difference between a manual breakpoint and a virtual breakpoint?

options.text: There is no difference — they are the same thing.
Manual breakpoints are set explicitly by the user; virtual breakpoints are created automatically when debugging controls are used.
Manual breakpoints only work in production; virtual breakpoints only work locally.
Virtual breakpoints can only be set on API steps.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is placed by hand, the other appears as a side effect of using debugging tools.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Manual breakpoints are set by the user; virtual breakpoints are created automatically by the system when debugging controls (step into, step out, step over, pause) are used.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you run a test one step at a time to inspect it after each action?

options.text: Click the dropdown next to Play, select 'Run locally step by step', then use 'Play Next Step'.
This is not supported — tests always run start to finish.
Delete all steps except the one you want to inspect.

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a dedicated run mode for this.
practiceQuiz.rationale: To run step-by-step, click the dropdown next to the Play button, select 'Run locally step by step', then click 'Play Next Step' to execute the next step and inspect state in between.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After clicking Pause during a test run, what does clicking Continue do?

options.text: Restarts the entire test from the first step.
Resumes execution from the exact point it was paused, until the test ends.
Skips the remainder of the test entirely.

practiceQuiz.hint: It picks up exactly where it left off.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Continue resumes test execution from the current (paused) location until the test ends — it doesn't restart from the beginning, skip the rest, or open an unrelated panel.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester has isolated a failure to a custom validation step's JavaScript logic using Pause and step-by-step execution. Which of Testim's four debugging tools is the right next step for inspecting that code specifically?

options.text: Debugging Controls again, since it covers everything.
Recording New Steps to Resolve Bugs.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the tool specifically built for stepping through custom-step code.
practiceQuiz.rationale: JavaScript Code Debugging is the dedicated workflow for stepping through the hand-written or AI-generated code inside custom action/validation/CLI steps — the right tool once Debugging Controls has narrowed the failure down to a specific custom step's logic. Recording New Steps is for fixing the test afterward, not diagnosing code.
